newsitem.title: USA: U.S West spot power firms on temperatures, natgas.
newsitem.headline: U.S West spot power firms on temperatures, natgas.

text.p: Spot power prices in the western U.S. firmed slightly amid forecasts calling for colder weather along with higher natural gas prices, trade sources said Thursday.
"The move is based off gas and weather reports," said one trader.
Sources also the continued absence of on-peak offers from the Bonneville Power Administration helped support the regional spot power market.
Firm, peak California-Oregon border (COB) electricity for Friday was assessed at $23.00-24.00 per megawatt hour (MWH), up from $21.50-22.50 for Thursday.
Firm, off-peak COB power for Friday was unchanged at $14.00-15.00.
Friday firm, peak power at Mid-Columbia (Mid-C) was slightly higher at $20.00-21.00. Off-peak Mid-C was also up at $15.00-16.00.
Firm, peak Palo Verde (PV) electricity for Friday was quoted $23.50-25.00 per MWh, up from $22.00-23.00. Firm off-peak PV was unchanged at $14.00-15.00.
Friday firm, peak prices at Four Corners were also slightly higher at $23.00-24.00, while firm off-peak was assessed at $14.00-16.00.
